Occasions

Every occasion plans differently

A proposal and a conference are both events, and almost nothing about planning them is the same. Different lead times, different guest lists, different things that go wrong. Start with the occasion you are actually working on.

Get event planning quotesCompare planning services
  • Weddings, proposals, parties and corporate

Why does the occasion change the planning job so much?

Because the occasion sets the constraints, and the constraints set everything else. A wedding is a twelve month project with twelve suppliers and one immovable date. A proposal is a four to eight week project that has to stay secret from the person it is for. A kids party is a two hour window where the hardest problem is the order things happen in.

So the first useful question is not your budget or which planner you like. It is what kind of event you are running, because that tells you how early to start, how much help to buy and what to watch.

The other celebrations planners work on

No page of their own yet. Here is the short version of what changes for each.

Milestone birthdays

A fiftieth behaves more like a small wedding than a kids party: a venue, 60 to 120 guests, catering, drinks and speeches. The venue minimum spend decides everything.

Kids parties

Two hours, an activity in the middle and a hard finish. The planning is almost entirely the running order. Book the entertainer first, because Saturday mornings in term time go early.

Baby showers

Usually 20 to 40 guests, daytime, planned in six to eight weeks. The guest of honour is not meant to be the organiser, so the person booking help is often a sister or a friend. Say so when you enquire.

Christenings and naming days

The church or celebrant sets a time you do not control. Most families run two sites in one day, so the real work is the gap: how guests travel, how long the food waits, who lets the caterer into the second venue.

Anniversary parties

Usually organised by adult children, which makes the guest list the hard part: it spans four decades and nobody has current addresses. Plan for the room rather than the theme, with seating, sound, parking and an early start.

Private celebrations at home

Retirements, farewells and long lunches. A party at home is a logistics problem in a social disguise: where the hire truck parks, whether the caterer has power, and how the pack down happens unseen.

Two at once

Planning more than one occasion at the same time

Engaged couples often have three events running at once, and the order you lock them in matters.

A proposal, an engagement party and a wedding often land inside eighteen months of each other, competing for the same money, the same weekends and the same family goodwill. Couples who spend heavily on the engagement party and then meet the wedding budget usually wish they had done it the other way around.

Lock the wedding date and venue first, because it is the only one with real scarcity, then set the engagement party far enough back that the two do not blur. If a planner is doing more than one, say so when you enquire.

Not sure which help you need?

If nothing is booked, you want a planner. If most of it is booked and you want someone to run the day, you want a coordinator. The comparison guide draws the line properly.

Straight answers

Questions about occasions

Which occasions does Plan Your Event cover?

Weddings, proposals, engagement parties, milestone birthdays, kids parties, baby showers, christenings, anniversaries, private celebrations and corporate events. Four have a guide here; the rest are covered by the same planners.

How far ahead should I start planning?

It depends on the occasion. Weddings need nine to fourteen months for full planning. Corporate events want four to nine months. Milestone birthdays, engagement parties and anniversaries sit at three to four months. Proposals, kids parties and baby showers are commonly planned inside six to ten weeks.

Do I need a planner, or just someone for the day?

Look at how much is already booked. With nothing but a date and a guest count, a planner builds the whole thing. If the venue and suppliers are locked in and you simply cannot host and manage at once, on-the-day coordination is the better buy.

Can one planner handle two events for the same family?

Often yes. Planners who take an engagement party and the wedding together build the guest list, the supplier shortlist and the budget once rather than twice. Mention both when you enquire.

What if my occasion is not on this list?

Describe it in your own words. Retirements, graduations, memorials, club functions and family reunions are planned by the same people. What planners need is the date, the location, the guest count and how much you want to hand over.
